subject: [Action] Ridgecrest on-prem cluster segmentation + storage fallback plan

Subject: Ridgecrest on-prem cluster segmentation + storage fallback plan

Ian / Sam —

Thanks again for the kickoff this morning. Per our discussion I pulled together the sequence we'll need to lock down before we schedule the on-site delivery window:

1) Network segmentation: management VLAN + workload VLANs + optional vendor-proxy lane for model updates. We'll need the CIDR ranges for each lane and whether the site requires NAT egress through a single egress IP (for allowlisting).

2) Node classes: you mentioned two node types — 1x GPU pool (A100-class) for inference and 1x dense CPU pool for batch/aux jobs. Please confirm expected pod density per GPU node (avg concurrent requests) and whether you want preemptible-style burst nodes.

3) Persistent storage & PV binding: two tiers — encrypted blockstore for model artifacts and NVMe-backed ephemeral for KV cache. Need retention and snapshot cadence for encrypted blockstore.

4) Fallback model variants: when GPU capacity is constrained we recommend a quantized CPU-compatible variant with prefix caching. We'll document the expected latency delta; this matters for SLOs.

I'm attaching a quick topology sketch and a working SOW draft. Can you confirm the CIDRs and whether your security team requires inbound mgmt-only access via bastion (we can arrange a read-only ops account and limited port rules)?

Next steps: once you confirm the CIDRs and PV retention policy I'll loop in our Delivery Engineering owner and propose a two-week canary followed by full cutover.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez

Date: Tue, 13 Aug 2029 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ridgecrest on-prem cluster segmentation + storage fallback plan

Sergio —

Thanks for the note and clear checklist. Quick answers below:

- CIDRs: management 10.100.0.0/24, workload 10.100.1.0/22, vendor-proxy 10.100.2.0/28.
- Egress: prefer single NAT egress IP for outbound allowlisting; we'll provide the firewall rule once the cutover week is set.
- Node density: target 4 concurrent inference pods per A100 node (p95 spikes to ~8). We'll expect sustained 200 rps during peak.
- Burst nodes: yes, we want an autoscale pool of preemptible GPUs for burst capacity but cannot rely on them for SLA-critical traffic.
- Storage retention: encrypted blockstore (30d snapshots, weekly backups to on-site tape archive) — encryption keys managed by our HSM; we will provide access policies.

Security note: our security team requires the management VLAN to be reachable only from the bastion. We cannot expose kube-api to the public internet.

I'll review the SOW and get you any procurement contacts by EOD.

— Ian
Ian Moore
Head of Infrastructure, Ridgecrest Systems

Subject: Re: Ridgecrest on-prem cluster segmentation + storage fallback plan

Quick technical notes based on Ian's constraints:

- Network: we'll recommend a dedicated nodePort range and a clusterCIDR that does not overlap your existing environment. We'll require static routes for the vendor-proxy lane so model pulls are auditable.

- PV classes:
  * fast-ephemeral (local NVMe): for KV cache, no snapshot, ephemeral restore only.
  * encrypted-block (iSCSI/LVM): for models and stateful workloads, snapshot every 24h (retention 30d). Must support KMS integration (HSM).

- Storage binding & eviction: set pod disruption budgets and local-storage eviction thresholds at 75% to avoid noisy-neighbor evictions during sustained peaks.

- Fallback plan: implement a routing policy at the service mesh edge: primary -> GPU pool; fallback -> quantized-cpu variant with checksum-based prefix caching. We expect p95 latency to increase by ~3-4x for heavy prompts but median should remain within application tolerances. We'll provide a calibration run during canary.

- Canary suggestion: 2-week canary with 10% production traffic routing to the new cluster, progressive ramp to 50% if latency/ops look good.

I'll prepare an ops-runbook snippet for the bastion access pattern and a short checklist for HSM key exchange.

— Neha

Subject: Re: Ridgecrest on-prem cluster segmentation + storage fallback plan

Ian —

Perfect, thanks for the CIDRs and retention guidance. Summary & immediate asks so procurement can move:

- We will update the SOW to state: management VLAN 10.100.0.0/24 (bastion-only), workload 10.100.1.0/22, vendor-proxy 10.100.2.0/28; single egress IP for outbound allowlisting.
- Delivery will provision: 6x A100-equivalent GPU nodes (baseline), 3x preemptible GPU nodes for burst, and 8x CPU-dense nodes for batch/worker pools.
- Storage: encrypted-block PV class with 24h snapshot schedule (30d retention) + local NVMe ephemeral tier for KV cache. HSM integration required.
- Canary window: target week of Sep 9, 2029 for start; two-week progressive rollout.

Please review the updated SOW link and approve via DocuSign so we can lock hardware procurement timelines: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/RD-8793-SOW

If security needs an additional attestation (e.g., SOC2 evidence for our delivery subprocess), Marissa can share the packet.

I'll schedule a short 30-minute alignment call with delivery on Fri to run through the runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this staged.

— Sergio
